extraFacts.fact: SAE J1926 (ISO 11926) covers straight-thread O-ring boss (ORB) ports, where an O-ring sits at the port face and seals against the fitting; SAE J1453 (ISO 8434-3) covers O-ring face seal (ORFS) fittings, where the O-ring sits in a groove in a flat face. Standard O-rings are AS568 dash sizes: the 9xx series (-902 to -932) for ORB ports and the 0xx series (-011 to -029) for ORFS.
extraFacts.source: SAE J1926-1 / ISO 11926-1; SAE J1453 / ISO 8434-3; SAE AS568 (uniform dash numbers for O-rings)

extraFacts.fact: Nitrile (NBR) is the standard O-ring elastomer for mineral-oil hydraulic fluid and is typically rated to about 100 degrees C. Fluoroelastomer (FKM, trade name Viton) is typically rated to about 200 degrees C and resists a wider range of fluids and heat, but ratings depend on the compound, so confirm the compound for the fluid and temperature.
extraFacts.source: Parker O-Ring Handbook ORD 5700 (elastomer properties); ISO 1629 rubber designations NBR and FKM

extraFacts.fact: An O-ring seals by being compressed, so it takes a set once used and a new one should be fitted whenever a joint is remade. A nicked, twisted or dry-rolled O-ring is the usual cause of a leak at an ORB or ORFS joint.
extraFacts.source: SAE J1453 and J1926 assembly practice

extraFacts.fact: Rubber O-rings are normally classified under HS subheading 4016.93 (gaskets, washers and other seals of vulcanised rubber); the importer's customs broker has the final say.
